pairs.difference: A: the witch hat is near-black with almost no hue. The lens shows the cone and brim as one charcoal-violet mass, and the only colors on the hat are a purple band and a yellow buckle. Behind it is an acid-green ring background, louder than any real card. Subject chroma is 0.039 and shadow chroma kept is 0.44, both below the real range. B: the cap keeps a rich navy body with violet-blue shadows and one orange-gold tassel accent against a cyan ring background, which matches the real pattern of a colored hero on a related, colored background.
pairs.fix: Paint the hat in deep plum-purple felt instead of black, with shadows that stay violet and never go gray. Make the green background softer and lighter so the hat is the loudest thing on the card.

pairs.difference: A: a large flat gray stone counter covers the bottom half of the card. It is a dead neutral mass that no real card has. The brass candlestick reads olive-khaki in the lens, the candle is gray-white, and only the flat cyan wall carries color. Background chroma is 0.093, below real. B: a saturated blue machine on a magenta-violet room, with pink, yellow and green cans as small accents. It is loud, but it fits the real two-hue hero-against-background setup.
pairs.fix: Replace the gray counter with a warm honey-wood tabletop. Make the brass warm gold with orange-brown shadows, and give the candle a creamy ivory body.

pairs.difference: A: the potion liquid is pushed to pure electric violet and fills most of the subject, with violet carried into the cast shadow on the table. Subject chroma is 0.196, above the real range. A lime cork adds a second, unrelated pure hue. B: the beach ball keeps cream-white panels and moderate red, blue and green, and the shadow shifts to a related red-orange on the sand, as real cards do.
pairs.fix: Tone the potion to a deeper grape purple with darker plum shadows and whiter glass highlights. Use a natural tan cork, and keep the table shadow brown, not purple.

pairs.difference: A: a pure-black cauldron (subject chroma 0.04) sits between a hot-pink background and acid-green grass and slime. Two maximum-chroma complementary fields surround a hueless hero, and the cauldron's shadows are flat black-green. Background chroma is 0.200, above the real range. B: the red mower keeps red-to-maroon shadows on a cyan background with green grass, which reads as natural local color.
pairs.fix: Paint the cauldron in dark iron with a cool blue-violet sheen and colored rim highlights. Make the pink background a softer, dustier rose, and turn the slime to a less neon green.

pairs.difference: A: the bare brown tree turns olive-gold in its lit planes in the lens, and one pure orange leaf is a lone accent. The scene is three flat bands: cyan sky, lime grass, brown trunk. B: the topiary keeps several green steps from yellow-green to deep green, with a neutral stone ring and a warm path as a resting area. The evidence is weak either way.
pairs.fix: Give the trunk reddish-brown bark with cool violet-brown shadows instead of olive highlights. Use a softer, slightly warmer grass, and add a few muted leaves on the ground.

pairs.difference: A: a cream marble lion in a green park, with low subject chroma that fits white stone, and a warm brick path for balance. B: a saturated blue bottle on a yellow-orange sunburst, a classic real complementary setup, though the background runs a little loud. Neither card breaks the real color pattern clearly.

B: the pumpkin is one orange mass. Its shadows only darken the same orange instead of shifting toward red-brown or violet, and the lit carving is also orange-yellow. The violet sunburst is pushed hard: background chroma 0.234, above the real range. A: the jacket mixes muted tan, orange cuffs and a dark green sash on a green burst, with natural local colors and a neutral rest area in the tan cloth.
pairs.fix: Shade the pumpkin with deep red-brown in its grooves and a cool violet tint on the shadow side. Make the purple background lighter and less saturated so the pumpkin stands out.

pairs.difference: A: the coaster cars are primary yellow and red on a cobalt track against a cyan sky. Subject chroma is 0.173, above the real range, and the lens shows the cars as flat red masses with no neutral rest. B: the cream scroll with a red ribbon and gold seal sits on a blue table, a neutral hero with one warm accent, as on real cards. The evidence is weak.
pairs.fix: Make the cars a softer sunny yellow with orange shadows, use a less saturated blue for the track, and add more white cloud area.

pairs.difference: B: the ghost sheet's shadows go lilac-purple, the pumpkin goes purple in the lens, and the violet sky casts its hue over the whole card. Background chroma is 0.154, above the real range, and the warm share is low. A: the pool sheep keeps a white fleece with cool shadows, a yellow float, teal water and green foliage, so each object keeps its own local color.
pairs.fix: Keep the sheet white with soft blue-gray shadows. Paint the pumpkin true orange with brown grooves, and make the sky a calm daytime blue with only a hint of lavender.

pairs.difference: B: a brown bat on an orange sunburst, with warm share 1.0 and only 1.78 hue families, below the real range. The whole card is one orange-brown family, the wings are brown-on-orange with no hue contrast, and the shadows are orange-brown. A: the jellyfish is magenta-pink against a deep blue sea, with cyan accents and blue-shifted shadows, a clear hero-against-background hue split.
pairs.fix: Put the bat on a cool purple or teal sunburst. Give the wings a dusky violet-brown membrane and the fur a warm brown, with pink only on the ears.

pairs.difference: B: the candy corn is three flat pure bands, white, orange and yellow, and its cast shadow on the wood is a saturated orange of the same hue as the stripe. The white tip reads mint in the lens. The card is mostly flat orange and yellow against flat blue stripes. A: the fruit plate has varied local colors (red watermelon, orange, green grapes, blue berries) and greenish-glass neutrals, and the shadows stay a muted olive-brown.
pairs.fix: Make the cast shadow a soft brown-gray on the wood instead of orange. Give the candy a waxy cream tip and slightly muted orange and yellow bands with gentle darker edges.

pairs.difference: A: the cottage walls and roof are one dull gray-lavender, with subject chroma 0.054, at the bottom of the real range. They sit against a hard cyan sky and lime grass (background chroma 0.158, above the real range), and the windows are the only warm accent. The hero is the quietest thing on the card. B: red brick, warm copper gate and peach paving against blue sky and green trees give a coherent warm hero on a cool background.
pairs.fix: Paint the cottage stone a warm lilac with a deep plum roof and violet shadows. Make the sky and grass softer and less saturated so the house carries the color.

pattern: The generated cards are the horror-themed props: witch hat, cauldron, candle, potion, pumpkin, ghost, bat, candy corn and cottage. They give themselves away in four ways. (1) Many heroes are near-black or gray, like the hat, the cauldron and the cottage walls, and they sit on maximum-chroma backgrounds such as acid green, hot pink or hard cyan, so the background is louder than the hero. (2) Some cards collapse into one hue family: the bat on orange, the orange pumpkin, the candy corn on wood. (3) Shadows only darken the same hue (orange to darker orange) or go gray-black instead of shifting to a related red-brown or violet. (4) Pure neon accents like the violet potion and lime cork are dropped in with no neutral area to rest the eye. On real cards the hero keeps a colored, natural local color (navy rather than black, tan rather than flat orange). The background shares or complements its hue at equal or lower loudness, and shadows keep their chroma with a hue shift.
